  raise ff                               friends & family: +$40K for 10% (2 Bandwidth, until 2018Q2)
  raise seed                             seed investors: +$1.5M for 20% (2 Bandwidth, 2017Q4–2019Q4, needs a quarter of mining)
  raise a                                Series A: +$8M for 20% (2 Bandwidth, 2019Q1–2021Q2, needs 1 MW powered across your sites)
  raise ipo                              IPO / SPAC: +$150M for 15% (3 Bandwidth, 2021, needs 20 MW and $3M quarterly EBITDA)
  pitch seed|a                           pitch the round for a higher valuation instead (2 Bandwidth, lost if no deal), then:
  counter <$M> · accept · walk           e.g. "counter 6.6" (pre-money valuation in $ millions)
  leave <site#>                          break a site's lease: 1 month's rent, its machines are sold
  loan <amount>                          borrow against your machines, e.g. "loan 5000" (1 Bandwidth)
  repay [construction|bridge]            pay the equipment (or construction, or bridge) loan off early
  cloan <btc|eth> <amount>               pledge treasury coins and borrow, e.g. "cloan eth 5000" (1 Bandwidth, 2018Q1–2022Q2)
  crepay                                 repay the crypto loan and get the coins back
  renew <site#> [fixed|index]            accept a due power contract renewal's opening offer (0 Bandwidth)
  negotiate <site#> [4|8] [fixed|index]  negotiate a due renewal instead (2 Bandwidth), then:
  counter <cents> · accept · walk        e.g. "counter 5.2" (price in ¢/kWh)
  hire <1-7> · fire <1-7>                1 Ops Manager, 2 Trader, 3 BD Lead, 4 Ex-Utility Exec, 5 Chief of Staff; Act II: 6 Head of Development, 7 Capital Markets Lead (hire: 1 Bandwidth + a quarter's salary in cash)
  read                                   read the market: a BTC/ETH hint for this quarter (1 Bandwidth, 0 with the Trader)
  talk <site#>                           talk to the neighbours there: cash + 1 Bandwidth, lowers Heat
  mitigate <site#>                       noise mitigation there: base Heat -10 for good (once per site)
  sellcoins <btc|eth> <1-100>            sell that % of a coin in the treasury, e.g. "sellcoins eth 50" (1 Bandwidth)
  bid <amount> [site#]                   sealed bid for this quarter's distressed auction lot (2 Bandwidth)
  host <site#> <kW>                      Act II: rent free power at a site to other miners, $0.1M per MW, live next quarter (1 Bandwidth)

  project <site#> <kW> shell|cloud|pilot [h100|h200|b200] [grid|gas]  Act II: open an AI project on free MW, or on new grid / gas power (1 Bandwidth)

ui.loan.rating_note: Priced on your credit rating ({rating}): SOFR plus the spread for that band, {apr} a year, up to {ltv} of the collateral. A better rating when you borrow means a cheaper, bigger loan.
ui.loan.max: Lenders go up to {ltv} of that
ui.loan.payment: About {value} a quarter to start with (principal plus interest), for {quarters} quarters.
ui.plan.crypto_loan_offer: Crypto-backed loan · {ltv} of coin value at {apr}
ui.cloan.title: Crypto-backed loan
ui.cloan.note: Pledge coins from your treasury and borrow up to {ltv} of their value, at {apr} a year (paid weekly). Repay whenever you like to get the coins back. If the coin's price falls, the loan-to-value (LTV) rises: at {call} the lender makes a margin call, at {liquidation} it sells your coins.
ui.cloan.danger: Margin call if {coin} falls to {call} (now {price}); forced sale at {liquidation}.
ui.hires.title: People
ui.hires.note: Hiring costs {bw} Bandwidth and needs a quarter's salary in cash. Salaries are paid weekly and count in EBITDA. Letting someone go is free in Bandwidth but costs a quarter's salary, and you can't rehire them the same quarter.
ui.margin_warning.title: Your Trader flags the crypto loan
ui.margin_warning.body: Your {coin} loan ({balance}) is at {ltv} LTV. A margin call comes at 70%. Repay it now, or carry on and watch the price.
ui.community.title: Neighbours and noise
ui.community.note: Talking to the neighbours ({bw} Bandwidth) buys goodwill: grievance {grievance}, at most once per site per quarter. Noise mitigation ({mbw} Bandwidth) lowers a site's base Heat by {base} for good, once per site.
ui.complaint.title: The neighbours are complaining about the {tier}
ui.complaint.body: Fans at night, trucks at dawn, a power bill that went up. Heat at the {tier} is {heat}. Settle it, fix the noise for good, or let it build.
ui.complaint.source: Hood County TX and upstate NY noise disputes. One complaint a quarter at most, from Heat {at}.
ui.auction.title: Distressed auction
ui.auction.note: A failed miner's machines, sold as one lot: {value} at the used price. Minimum bid {reserve}. Needs {power} of free space at one site.
ui.auction.profit: Each earns {value}/day at the {tier} at today's prices.
ui.auction.rules: One bid only. The highest bid wins and pays what it bid; a tie goes to the rival. Win or lose, the bid costs the Bandwidth. Used machines arrive at once and earn from next quarter.
ui.signals.title: Signals
ui.signals.headline: Headline · {quarter}
ui.tip.q1_welcome_prologue: January 2017. You have {cashUsd}, {machines} machines, {btc} and a garage. You're doing this full-time now. Bitcoin is $1,000; how fast you can sell is limited, so most of it stays on paper.
ui.signals.read_market: Read the market ({bw} Bandwidth) hints whether BTC and ETH rise or fall more than {up} this quarter.
ui.read.result: Your read for this quarter: {btc} · {eth} (▲ ▼ = a move of more than {pct}).
ui.read.accuracy: Reads are right about {pct} of the time, and never off by more than one step.
read_flavour.up: Desks are whispering about fresh money coming in.
read_flavour.flat: The chatter is noncommittal: nobody wants to call it.
read_flavour.down: Lenders are getting nervous, and so are the forums.
error.market_read_done: You've already read the market this quarter.
error.market_read_act3: In 2027 you read the Signals panel instead.
error.signal_unavailable: The Signals panel only exists in Act III.
error.signal_unknown: There is no such Signals indicator.
error.signal_read_done: You've already read a Signals indicator this quarter.
ui.buy.title: Buy machines
ui.buy.profit_note: Profit per unit per day at this week's prices, on {site} power. Used machines break down more often.
ui.fleet_dialog.title: Your machines
ui.fleet_dialog.note: Machines sell at the used price. Broken ones go first, for the used price minus the repair cost.
ui.leave.title: Leave the {tier}?
ui.leave.note: Breaking the lease costs one month of rent. Rent stops from this quarter. It costs no Bandwidth.
ui.leave.machines: Sell {n} machine(s) there at the used price
ui.offers.title: Site offers
ui.offers.note: Each offer hides one flaw. You find out what it is when you build.
ui.offers.contract: Power contract for the new site:
ui.offers.financed_hint: Construction loan: borrow {loan} (60% of the cost, 11% a year, 8 quarters) and pay {cash} now.
ui.live.hodl_note: Selling {btc} of mined BTC and {eth} of mined ETH as they come in.
ui.uri.title: A deep freeze is coming to Texas
ui.uri.body: Week {week}: the grid is short of power and prices are about to hit the cap. Honour your curtailment deal: take the Texas site's {mw} offline and collect {credit} in credits. Or keep mining: an index contract then pays {price}/MWh on its whole contracted load for the week, even if the machines switch off. A fixed contract is unaffected.
ui.uri.effect_mine: Storm charge {charge} on index contracts · fixed contracts mine as usual (about {forgone}) · grievance {grievance}
ui.uri.source: Winter Storm Uri, Feb 2021: ERCOT prices sat at the $9,000/MWh cap for days. Index contracts earn 1.5× curtailment credits.
ui.grid.title: The Texas grid asks you to switch off
ui.grid.body: A heat wave is straining the grid. Take the Texas site's {mw} offline for week {week} and the grid pays {credit} in credits. Mining that week would earn about {forgone}.
ui.grid.ai_line: Your AI halls there ({power}) go dark that week too: their tenants get {sla} of SLA credits.
ui.grid.forced: SB6: ERCOT can now curtail sites of 75 MW and up directly. This time it isn't asking.
ui.spot_alert.spot_price_shock.title: Compute Just Got Cheaper
ui.spot_alert.spot_price_shock.body: A big cloud just cut its GPU rental prices: spot GPU-hours move {change} this afternoon.
ui.spot_alert.spot_price_shock.effect.lo: Every GPU-hour of your spot clusters sold at the new, lower price for {quarters} quarters, whatever the demand.
ui.spot_alert.spot_price_shock.effect.st: Spot prices at the new level for the rest of the quarter; after that, the market's.
ui.spot_alert.gpu_spot_alert.title: H100 Spot Price Alert
ui.spot_alert.gpu_spot_alert.body: The H100 spot price moved {change} this week. Your clusters on spot earn the neocloud price times their utilisation.
ui.spot_alert.gpu_spot_alert.effect.lock: Lock today's neocloud price on every GPU-hour of your spot clusters for {quarters} quarters.
log.spot_shock_silent: A spot price shock: prices for GPU-hours fell for the rest of the quarter (no time to act).
log.spot_locked: Spot capacity locked in for {quarters} quarters.
ui.grid.effect_curtail: {credit} in credits · gives up about {forgone} of mining, and saves the power
ui.grid.effect_mine: Earns about {forgone} · no credits · grievance {grievance} at the Texas site
ui.grid.source: Credits pay the bigger of $15K per MW or 1.25× the mining revenue given up (Texas demand response).
ui.margin.title: Your lender wants more collateral
ui.margin.body: {coin} fell and your loan of {balance} is now {ltv} of the pledged coins' value. Bring it back to {target} this week, or the lender sells your coins at {liquidation}.
ui.margin.effect_default: Lose {coins} ({value}) · {balance} written off · no loans for {quarters} quarters

ui.report.cash_line: Cash: start {start} + coin sales {sales} − power {power} − rent {rent} = end {end}.

ui.report.storm_line: Winter Storm Uri: storm power charge {usd} (included in power).
ui.report.debt_line: Still owed on the equipment loan: {debt} (interest this quarter: {interest}).

hire_bio.capital_markets_lead: Spent a decade selling infrastructure debt; knows which lender blinks first.

hire_effect.head_of_development: +1 Bandwidth every quarter, from next quarter (maximum 8).

ui.merge.body: Ethereum switches to proof-of-stake. From today, GPU mining pays nothing. What does your company become?

ui.gpuwave.title: GPU failures at project {n}
ui.gpuwave.body: {gpus} of the {cluster} GPUs in project {n}'s cluster at the {tier} failed at once. Big clusters lose a slice of their GPUs every so often; a failed GPU earns nothing until it is replaced.
ui.gpuwave.cause: About half of such failures are GPU and memory faults; the rest are software, network and CPU.
ui.gpuwave.basis: Basis: Meta's Llama 3 training run, where about 0.9% of a 16,384-GPU cluster failed over 54 days.
ui.gpuwave.effect_replace: {cash} to replace them now · no lost revenue
ui.gpuwave.effect_short: No cash now · they earn nothing for the rest of the quarter and the next · {cost} to replace them, paid at the end of next quarter
ui.gpuwave.effect_short_contract: No cash now · they earn nothing for the rest of the quarter and the next, and your tenant gets an SLA credit of {mult} the lost revenue · {cost} to replace them, paid at the end of next quarter

event.a3_67061add.title: A Softer Quote
event.a3_67061add.body: Your broker says two hyperscaler RFPs closed at rates a shade under last year's. Nobody is panicking; everyone is 'checking the model.'
event.a3_f8b4808a.title: Spreads Blink
event.a3_f8b4808a.body: A lender pulls a $600M deal, and DDTL spreads jump 200bp in a week. By Friday, two others quietly close at the old price. It looks like a signal. It may be noise.
event.a3_f8b4808a.choice.c1: Refinance now at the wider spread
event.a3_f8b4808a.choice.c3: Draw down the revolver as insurance
event.a3_eb5b36ca.title: The Digestion Quarter
event.a3_eb5b36ca.body: Two of the biggest cloud buyers say they will digest capacity already contracted. The first big neocloud master lease comes up: same tenant, same GPUs, 20-30% off shell rent and a two-year-longer ask. Not a crisis. Just the market.
event.a3_d5af698a.title: Everyone Reads the Same Report
event.a3_d5af698a.body: An analyst note says the reset was 'fully priced.' Your lender agrees; your tenant's CFO nods along. You feel oddly relieved.
event.a3_651ee74a.title: The Halving Trims the Miners
event.a3_651ee74a.body: Block subsidy halves again. Your older ASICs are underwater unless power is cheap. Most of the market saw it coming.
event.a3_c5f70e5e.title: A Good Year For Boring
event.a3_c5f70e5e.body: Your hedged sites collect the same rent for the fifth quarter running. The other players are still arguing about 2027.
event.a3_74f91ebe.title: A Cheaper Chip for Everyone
event.a3_74f91ebe.body: Rubin supply loosens. Hopper rent falls again. Old fleets earn less; new fleets are easier to fill.
event.a3_ae7659d3.title: Feynman Whispers
event.a3_ae7659d3.body: A trade blog says the next generation is 'a step change.' Rubin resale wobbles 3%.
event.a3_e84ea420.title: Your Lender Asks About Concentration
event.a3_e84ea420.body: A credit officer asks how much of your rent comes from one tenant. Politely. Twice. It is on the agenda for the annual review.
event.a3_e5723b9c.title: Chips Suddenly Scarce
event.a3_e5723b9c.body: New-generation racks are 30 weeks out and every neocloud is on the phone. You read it as demand. It could be a supply hiccup at one packager.
event.a3_cafecee9.title: The Round That Didn't Close
event.a3_cafecee9.body: An anchor AI lab's funding round fails to close and it misses two payments, citing financing conditions. Its sub-tenants are being called by lenders. Cap rates gap 100bp in a month.
event.a3_cafecee9.choice.c1: Renegotiate now: take a haircut to keep the tenant
event.a3_cafecee9.choice.c3: Buy the debt at a discount (if cash)
event.a3_cb774cd6.title: Refinancing Window Closes
event.a3_cb774cd6.body: Your DDTL matures in two quarters. New quotes are +250bp and 60% advance rate.
event.a3_03c3bdf0.title: The Backstop Was Real
event.a3_03c3bdf0.body: A hyperscaler that guaranteed your tenant's lease pays out. You are made whole. The guarantee cost you 5% of the company two years ago.
event.a3_a92ada1c.title: Distressed Sites Go To Auction
event.a3_a92ada1c.body: A leveraged rival's 60MW site goes under the hammer at $3M/MW. Stabilised EV/MW is down 55%.
event.a3_b89ee21f.title: Tenant Default Notice
event.a3_b89ee21f.body: A sub-tenant defaults on 30MW. Your take-or-pay claim is only as good as its parent.
event.a3_2d72100e.title: Chips Are Cheap Now
event.a3_2d72100e.body: Rubin racks trade at a 40% discount to 2027 list. The survivors are buying.
event.a3_403311b7.title: The Grid Is Nervous
event.a3_403311b7.body: The RTO's reserve-margin forecast just got worse. Load studies show your peers' interconnection requests doubling. Time to lock in energized MW.
event.a3_67d0f5fe.title: Efficiency Papers Everywhere
event.a3_67d0f5fe.body: Three labs publish 'do more with less' results in a week. Your GPU vendor's shares dip 8%. Is demand cracking?
event.a3_eb2dad54.title: Compute Is Strategic
event.a3_eb2dad54.body: Hyperscaler capex is guided up 35% and every energized MW is spoken for. The queue is five years. Spot prices explode; your renewals hold flat.
event.a3_eb2dad54.choice.c1: Sign a 10-yr lock with your best tenant
event.a3_eb2dad54.choice.c2: Go to spot on uncontracted MW
event.a3_4626269a.title: The Winners' Curse
event.a3_4626269a.body: A rival announces a $12B campus. Analysts note that the winner of last year's bidding is now paying 40% more for turbines.
event.a3_35d7cfb2.title: Nuclear Restart Pays
event.a3_35d7cfb2.body: Your fixed-price PPA looks like a gift as PJM power triples.
event.a3_4ba8a02a.title: Ratepayers Push Back
event.a3_4ba8a02a.body: Bills are up 30% in your region. A moratorium bill has 12 co-sponsors.
event.a3_c7c9d54d.title: New-Contract Premium
event.a3_c7c9d54d.body: New RFPs are clearing at +30%. Your old locked contracts look cheap. Tenants want to renew early and stay.
event.a3_1363a916.title: Too Good To Last?
event.a3_1363a916.body: Headlines say 'no bubble.' Your lender asks what you would do if it did.
event.a3_8b8fea85.title: Benchmarks Look Wrong
event.a3_8b8fea85.body: A new model matches frontier scores on one-tenth the compute. Engineers you know are quietly rewriting their capacity plans.
event.a3_d85e34b1.title: Grid Margin Collapses
event.a3_d85e34b1.body: A heat wave drops your reserve margin to 4%. Utilities warn of curtailment. It looks like scarcity. It is a weather week.
event.a3_791a5106.title: Open-Weights Week
event.a3_791a5106.body: A lab releases open weights matching frontier scores on one-tenth the GPUs. Chip lead times collapse from 18 to 6 weeks and hyperscalers cut capex 30%.
event.a3_791a5106.choice.c1: Ask tenants to reopen for shorter terms
event.a3_165d3111.title: The Reopener
event.a3_165d3111.body: Your tenant's contract has a market-reopener clause. They are using it.
event.a3_b13c83fe.title: Jevons Returns
event.a3_b13c83fe.body: Cheaper inference brings more use. AI demand index climbs 8 points in a quarter.
event.a3_3fd60c78.title: Flexible Is King
event.a3_3fd60c78.body: Your short-term contracts re-let within a month at the new price; long-locked neighbours are still stuck.
event.a3_f35eaca5.title: Chip Glut
event.a3_f35eaca5.body: Rubin racks are 30% off list. Inventories are heavy.
event.a3_9630ac97.title: Everyone Runs Small Models
event.a3_9630ac97.body: Edge inference is real. Regional sites near cities gain a small edge premium.
event.a3_22b90a0c.title: Act III Opens
event.a3_22b90a0c.body: The easy money is behind you. Your tenants are asking about 2028; your lenders are asking about 2027. Nobody can tell you what the market will do. Read the signals.
event.a3_c03ea202.title: Nuclear Offer
event.a3_c03ea202.body: A restarted reactor's owner offers a 15-year fixed PPA. No queue. Take-or-pay.
event.a3_c0e21850.title: Government Affairs Recruiter Calls
event.a3_c0e21850.body: A seasoned former commission aide is available.
event.a3_20531cf7.title: Rubin Ultra Preview
event.a3_20531cf7.body: The 600 kW rack is real. Existing halls cannot host it without a rebuild.
event.a3_f73f0237.title: The Reckoning Ends
event.a3_f73f0237.body: Four years of contracts and headlines. Time to see who read the market.

event.ec01_ftx_contagion.title: The Exchange That Wasn't
event.ec01_ftx_contagion.body: An exchange everyone trusted just imploded overnight. Crypto lenders freeze withdrawals, and every crypto-backed loan desk has gone dark. Your coins are worth a lot less by Monday.

act3.reveal.s0.trigger: In April 2028, just as the fifth halving lands, two of the four biggest cloud buyers tell investors they will 'digest' capacity already contracted and pause new leasing for a quarter. Nothing breaks: no tenant defaults and no lender leaves. But H100 and Blackwell rents fall 12-15% in a quarter, hyperscale cap rates back up about 45 bp, AI-infrastructure multiples lose roughly three turns and the AI demand index dips from 94 to 86. It proves to be a price reset rather than a crisis: rents stabilise within three quarters, and renewals on the calendar now price 20-30% below 2025 levels for good.
act3.reveal.s0.decoy_reason: A mid-size private-credit fund gates redemptions after a bad quarter in unrelated (software and consumer) loans. GPU-backed lenders pause new drawdowns for a few weeks and reprice the whole desk +100-225 bp. Tenant credit is unchanged and every existing contract keeps paying.
act3.reveal.s0.decoy_tell: Tenant CDS and lab revenue are flat while spreads spike; the move reverses within two quarters once the fund's redemptions are met. The card 'The Private Credit Wobble' names the cause.
act3.reveal.s1.trigger: In February 2028 a frontier AI lab that had pre-committed to more than $100B of compute fails to close a planned mega-round; its backers, facing their own marks, decline to fund it. Within weeks lab tenants invoke force-majeure clauses, a marquee GPU-backed loan is pulled from syndication and a wave of half-built campuses stalls. Over the next two quarters GPU spot prices fall 50-70%, hyperscale exit cap rates widen by 200+ bp, DDTL spreads double and lenders stop lending to neoclouds. Hyperscalers with signed leases keep paying, but stop signing new ones.
act3.reveal.s1.decoy_reason: A yield problem in HBM4 memory at one supplier plus a packaging-line outage stretch newest-generation lead times from 18 to 30 weeks. It is a supply-side squeeze, not a demand surge. Lab tenants quietly stop adding to their orders.
act3.reveal.s1.decoy_tell: Lead times rise while the Revenue Gap is widening and Lender Spreads are drifting up - scarcity plus weakening economics is not what a demand boom looks like. Spot rents do not follow lead times up.
act3.reveal.s2.trigger: In July 2028, after two consecutive quarters in which reported AI revenue outgrows capex, a federal order designates large AI compute campuses as critical infrastructure: it pre-empts local permitting on designated sites, fast-tracks interconnection for approved projects and opens a nuclear-licensing track. Frontier labs raise again at higher valuations, spot GPU prices climb despite new supply, and every energized megawatt becomes a scarce asset. Protests reach their highest intensity yet, over bills, water and land.
act3.reveal.s2.decoy_reason: An open-weights model matches frontier quality at about one-eighth the serving cost. Token prices fall sharply for six weeks. Usage then explodes (Jevons): new products launch, labs re-invest the savings in bigger runs, and compute demand ends the quarter higher, not lower.
act3.reveal.s2.decoy_tell: Efficiency jumps but the Revenue Gap keeps narrowing, chip lead times keep lengthening and spot rents keep rising - the savings are being spent, not banked.
act3.reveal.s3.trigger: In October 2027 an open-weights model matches frontier quality on the benchmarks that matter and can be served at about a tenth of the cost per token. Chip stocks fall double digits in a day and token prices collapse 8-10x. AI-lab tenants invoke 'material change' reopeners on contracts priced for scarce compute; hyperscalers hold their leases but tell you next year's orders will be trimmed. After four to six quarters, cheaper tokens unlock new uses and demand rebounds (the Jevons effect), mostly for newer chip generations and inference-optimised sites; older Hopper capacity never fully recovers.
act3.reveal.s3.decoy_reason: A record summer heat wave and two delayed plant retirements squeeze reserve margins in PJM and ERCOT. It is weather and supply, not AI load growth; hyperscaler load additions are actually flat that year.
act3.reveal.s3.decoy_tell: Reserve margins tighten with no matching rise in lead times, no narrowing of the Revenue Gap and no rise in spot rents. Capacity prices spike for two quarters, then ease.
